title: The assistant that forgot the price list
scenario:
You run a small sales team. Your manager wants to use an AI chat assistant to draft replies to customer emails. In a trial, a teammate asks the assistant: "What is our discount for orders over 500 units?" The assistant answers with a number. Nobody gave it the company price list. A second teammate asks the same question and gets a different number.

Your manager asks you to explain what happened and what to change before the team uses the tool.

questions.prompt: Why could the assistant not know the real discount?

options.text: The price list was never in its context window, and a company's own price list is not something it learned in training.
options.explanation: Right. The model works from its training plus what is in its context window, its "working memory". Your private price list was in neither.

options.text: The assistant has a bug and needs to be reinstalled.
options.explanation: Nothing is broken. The model wrote a fluent answer without the facts it needed. Reinstalling gives it no price list.

options.text: The assistant's training data is too old. A newer model would know the discount.
options.explanation: No model's training data includes your private price list, however new the model is. OpenAI's accuracy guide lists proprietary information as a gap you must fill yourself.

options.text: AI assistants can look up any company's internal files on their own.
options.explanation: A model only sees what is in its context window. Here nobody gave it the file, so it had nothing to look up.

questions.prompt: Why did the two teammates get different numbers for the same question?

options.text: One teammate typed the question wrong.
options.explanation: They asked the same thing. Different answers to the same prompt are normal for LLMs, so a typo is not needed to explain it.

options.text: LLM output is non-deterministic: the same prompt can give different answers.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs call model output non-deterministic, and Anthropic's glossary says identical inputs may produce different outputs.

options.text: The model changed the company discount between the two questions.
options.explanation: The model can't change your prices. It wrote two different guesses because it had no real price list to read.

options.text: The second answer is the correct one because it came later.
options.explanation: Neither answer came from the price list. A later answer is not more true.

questions.prompt: What is the best change before the team uses the tool for customer emails?

options.text: Ask the question again until two answers match.
options.explanation: Two matching guesses are still guesses. The model still has no price list.

options.text: Stop using AI for any email, because it can't be trusted.
options.explanation: Too broad. Drafting replies is a good fit for an LLM. The fix is to give it the facts and check the drafts.

options.text: Give the assistant the current price list with each request, and have a person check prices in each draft before it is sent.
options.explanation: Right. Facts in the context window give the model something real to work from. A person still checks, because fluent text is not proof that the text is true.

options.text: Tell the assistant to write longer, more detailed replies.
options.explanation: More words do not add the missing facts. A longer reply can hold more wrong details.
